answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy makes every identity post a costly stake before it can act. Each agent locks funds in a vault that a peer jury can slash if it cheats, so flooding the network with raven-like copycat identities stops being free: every extra wallet the attacker spawns must deposit real collateral, and duplicate behavior burns that stake. Like pigment distinguishing a true signature from a forgery, unique per-agent work proofs make each identity expensive to fake, so the cost of N sybils scales linearly while honest gains stay flat.
